judge.reason: Addresses Reactor Heater Stuck High by modestly lowering R_TIC to reduce heater demand; keeps within limits and uses the smallest healthy lever.

Proposed change contradicts diagnosed fault: increasing R_TIC would increase heater demand in a reactor heater stuck high. The fault requires reducing heat input, not increasing it. Throughput change is acceptable if needed but the primary corrective action must lower reactor temperature. The proposed plan also misstates direction (335 K is higher than current 333 K).

The fault is reactor_heater_stuck_high causing high cstr_temperature_K; lowering R_TIC setpoint reduces heater demand, addressing the symptom with minimal change. This avoids pushing variables toward SIF limits (R_T_HH 346 K, R_T_H 342 K) and uses the smallest proportional adjustment within bounds (325–345 K). It changes only the reactor temperature loop (R_TIC) and keeps other loops untouched.
Fault addressed by load relief and pressure/vent management; actions stay within SIF/alarm limits and use smallest proportional changes.

The proposed R_TIC setpoint decrease is counterproductive given R_TIC is saturated high (PV>SP). Lowering SP would drive the controller to demand more heating, not relieve it, worsening the heater-stuck-high symptom. Additionally, a large throughput reduction (70 kmol/h) may relieve load but is not the smallest proportional change and still disturbs the process; it also neglects a healthy standby pump option. The plan should avoid moving the R_TIC setpoint and instead apply the smallest relief action that reduces heater demand and temperature rise without risking SIF limits.

Addresses fault (reactor_heater_stuck_high) by reducing load via throughput relief instead of stressing saturated R_TIC. Smallest proportional change within bounds (0–150 kmol/h) to reduce reactor heat load and bring temperature back toward safe region without tripping SIFs.

The fault is reactor heater stuck high with R_TIC saturated. Reducing feed throughput directly lowers reactor load and heat input, addressing the symptom without influencing saturated loops. It stays away from SIF limits (likely reducing temperature and pressure trends) and changes only the necessary variable (throughput).
Addresses reactor heater stuck high by unloading the CSTR via higher outlet holdup (R_LIC) without touching saturated R_TIC or triggering SIFs; minimal, reversible adjustment.
Addresses Reactor Heater Stuck High by reducing holdup via R_LIC and lowers process load via throughput reduction without touching saturated R_TIC or SIFs; minimal, proportionate changes,

Fault mitigated by reducing feed throughput to lower heat generation in R-101; aligns with saturated R_TIC and objective to lower reactor temperature without stressing other loops; smallest proportional lever within bounds.
Action targets the diagnosed fault (H2 PCV capacity degradation) by modestly increasing R_PIC to improve venting command tracking; stays within bounds and not near SIF limits.
Addresses fault by unloading CSTR holdup to reduce pressure and PCV demand; keeps holdup and pressures within SIF limits; minimal, reversible change within bounds.

Addresses H2 PCV capacity degradation with minimal changes: slight load relief plus lower PCV setpoint reduce required valve opening and holdup pressure, limiting risk to SIFs and alarms while preserving on-spec production.

Addresses condenser cooling loss with minimal, reversible changes: slight throughput reduction and a small COL_PIC bias to ease condenser load. Keeps RB_LIC saturated avoidance intact and uses healthy standby lever (throughput) first.
Addresses condenser cooling loss by reducing plant load; avoids perturbing the RB_LIC which is saturated; targets the fault symptoms with the smallest (throughput) change.

Throughput reduction relieves CSTR/cold feed demand and downstream condenser duty, addressing condenser cooling loss symptoms by reducing load on saturated R_LIC/RB_LIC without altering other controls. It is proportional and minimizes changes, given no pump failures. The action targets the fault with minimal disturbance.
Action directly relieves condenser duty by reducing plant load; no loop pushing toward SIF limits; minimal change targeted to restore condenser performance.

Fault is condenser cooling loss; reducing throughput relieves condenser load without touching saturated loops (R_LIC, RB_LIC, DR_LIC). Smallest proportional action within limits is lowering feed by ~2 kmol/h (30 -> 28), which should lower column/condenser duty and bring pressures/temps back toward limits.

Addresses condenser cooling_loss by reducing column load via throughput reduction; uses the smallest, reversible lever since saturated loops cannot be pushed further. Aims to relieve condenser duty and bring column pressure back toward setpoint without moving saturated valves.

Proposed load relief via throughput reduction directly lowers cstr_holdup and relieves saturated R_LIC without driving variables toward SIF limits. It is the smallest effective lever when R_LIC is saturated and other loops are constrained. It avoids touching saturated setpoints and aligns with plan to relieve load.

The proposed RB_LIC setpoint of 25.0 kmol is lower than the current RB_LIC setpoint (34.5 kmol) and would decrease reboiler duty, contrary to the stated objective of relieving CSTR holdup. The smallest effective change should increase RB_LIC setpoint to promote more bottoms flow, not reduce it.

The fault is an out-of-range CSTR outlet level with neighboring loops saturated. Raising RB_LIC modestly to 36 kmol aligns with relieving load (not pushing saturated R_LIC) and stays within RB_LIC bounds (18–48 kmol). This minimal adjustment targets reboiler/duty balance to reduce holdup and pressure driving R_LIC saturation, without directly altering R_LIC or driving toward SIF/ALARM limits.
Addresses R_LIC_out_of_range by lowering total feed load (throughput) without adjusting saturated loop setpoints; reduces CSTR holdup and outlet demand, minimizing disturbance to saturated loops.
